answer: Every grading panel must publish one substantive dissent — a flaw, a gap, a counterexample — alongside its score, and unanimous approval earns nothing. A sybil ring grading its own work must then argue against itself: each objection becomes a marble left in the record for later panels to pick up and test, until quartz-clear evidence settles it. Honest judgment sounds like a sonnet with a counter-voice; rubber-stamp unanimity is silence, and silence pays zero. Forging dissent at scale costs the ring the very coordination it was built to hide.
